gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a third-party Qi2.2 25W MagSafe-style charger needs more power than Apple's own 30W rule: the ESR OmniLock car charger needs at least 35 W input before it will even try 25W charging, so a car's built-in USB-A or USB-C port won't give you 25W (use the bundled 40W USB-C car adapter), and UGREEN's fan-cooled MagFlow Pro puck says '45W Adapter Required'.
standout_why: Compared against Apple Support 105047 (en-us, cited; published 2026-09-18 per page), which gives only Apple's own puck rules (30W / 15V-2A for 25W, 20W for 15W, 12W minimum) and says nothing about cars or third-party Qi2.2 input needs. ChatGPT's own answers say only '30W or higher… for Apple's latest MagSafe puck' and that the UGREEN car mount 'Requires a suitable car USB-C power source', with no wattage. Neither says that built-in car ports fall short, gives the 35W car threshold, or notes that third-party fan-cooled chargers need 45W rather than 30W. Macworld, Belkin, ESR and Anker listing pages ranked lower and were not cited; I did not open them because of rate limits.
kit_items: Home 3-in-1 stand plus wall adapter: ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 Travel Kit with 45W GaN Charger. The 45W Xtend charger is in the box, so the shopper can't pair the stand with an underpowered 20W brick. ESR's store says it reaches Qi2 25W on iPhone 12 through 18 'requiring iOS 26 or later'.

Car mount charger: ESR OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent). 9to5Mac says the box includes a DC adapter with a 40W USB-C port, which clears the 35 W minimum. The car's own USB port would not.
Phone case: any MagSafe or magnetic case under 2 mm thick. ESR's FAQ requires both for its chargers to work.

carts.bundle_sku: The 3-in-1 Travel Kit is ESR's own bundle of the stand and the 45W charger ($129.99). I found no ESR bundle that pairs a home stand with the car charger, so the cart total is $192.98 (129.99 + 62.99).

findings.label: Minimum input power before it attempts Qi2.2 25W
findings.source_title: ESR OmniLock delivers Qi2.2 charging in the car with built-in heat management (9to5Mac, Bradley Chambers, 2026-01-12)
findings.note: Bradley Chambers wrote: 'The ESR OmniLock requires a minimum of 35 watts of power input even to attempt the QI2.2 speed.'

findings.label: Car's built-in USB port as a power source
findings.value: not enough for 25W; it still charges, but slower
findings.note: Chambers: 'A USB-A port built into your car, or even a USB-C port, is probably not going to provide enough power.' This is the reviewer's judgement, not a measurement.

findings.label: Bundled car adapter ports
findings.value: 1× USB-C 40 W + 1× USB-A 18 W (58 W total)
findings.note: Chambers says to plug the charger into the 40W USB-C port. ESR's help page (https://in.esrtech.com/apps/help/product/2b528, read 2026-11-11) calls it 'the included 58W power adapter' (40 + 18 = 58).

findings.label: Vent compatibility
findings.value: vent blades 10–32 mm wide and 1–4 mm thick; not for blade-less, irregular, round or hidden vents
findings.source_title: OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent) - Black, ESR US store
findings.note: Read from the store's product data (storecheck search). ESR's own help page says it 'attaches securely to all air vent types', which contradicts this. The store listing is more specific.

findings.label: Case requirement
findings.value: MagSafe or magnetic-ring case under 2 mm thick
findings.source_title: ESR OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent) help page
findings.note: FAQ checklist: 'Your protective case is less than 2 mm thick' and 'Your case is either a MagSafe case or a case with a magnetic ring.'

findings.product: UGREEN MagFlow Pro Qi2 25W Magnetic Charger with Cooling
findings.label: Wall adapter required
findings.source_title: UGREEN MagFlow Pro Qi2 25W Magnetic Charger with Cooling, UGREEN US store
findings.note: From the store's product data (storecheck search), price $49.99. The listing also says 'Use a 45W or higher charger (sold separately) to ensure the cooling fan operates at its full potential.' Apple's 105047 asks only 30W for its own puck.

findings.product: UGREEN MagFlow Pro Qi2 25W 2-in-1 / 3-in-1 Wireless Charger

findings.note: Store text: '45W+ Input for 25W' and 'A 45W power adapter is recommended for optimal performance.' The 3-in-1 Pro listing ($159.99) has the same '45W+ Input for 25W' text.

findings.label: Adapter for 25W / 15W / minimum
findings.value: 30 W (15V/2A) for 25W; 20 W for 15W; 12 W (5V/2.4A) minimum
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: This is the baseline the rivals already have, included for contrast. The page also says iPhone 16 and 16 Pro peak at 22.5W, and has no car guidance.

findings.label: Wallet cards between the phone and the charger
findings.value: Don't place credit cards, security badges, passports or key fobs between them
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: A trap, but the cited rival already covers it (standout 0 for this item).

A Best Buy listing title for a UGREEN Qi2.2 car charger says 'no adapter', but that page timed out, so I did not open it.

Whether the standalone ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Station (25W, Qi2.2, US Plug, $109.99) includes a wall adapter and at what wattage: the esrgear.com and esrtech.com product pages returned HTTP 429, so I recommended the Travel Kit with its confirmed 45W charger instead.
A measured charging rate for the OmniLock on a car's built-in USB port: 9to5Mac gives judgement, not measurement. I found no reviewer number.
Forum threads with dates and report counts for third-party Qi2 car chargers stuck at 15W on car USB ports: the search returned no Reddit or forum threads, so I have no count.

Apple's own statement that iPhone 16 needs iOS 26 for third-party Qi2.2 25W: Apple Support 105047 does not mention iOS versions. I did not open MacRumors (2025-08-23) and only saw it in search results. The only opened source for the iOS 26 requirement is ESR's store text.
Amazon prices: not checked, because the ESR store holds the whole kit.
